increment_paragraph: **GATE-SLOT-ADMISSION-STARVATION** (round 25; USER DECISION 2026-11-06, verbatim: "Register it (rec.)"; requirement R11 of docs/plans/gate-time-reduction/README.md; [report](../../reports/gate-slot-admission-starvation/README.md)). scripts/gate_slot.py bounds the starvation observed on 2026-11-06 (an audit spinning 10 h 18 min with zero I/O while a rust-suite drain waited 10.1 h for its slot and every queued audit waited behind both). (1) Every slot job states its deadlines in its receipt: the script samples the command's process tree every 10 s and `--stall-timeout` stops it when no member changed its /proc/<pid>/io counters, started or ended and the `--progress-file` did not change for that long; `--deadline` is a wall-clock bound; defaults `audit` 2 h stall and no wall-clock deadline, `rust-suite` and `lean` neither (flag, else QUIRIN_GATE_STALL_TIMEOUT / QUIRIN_GATE_DEADLINE; a measured pinned-corpus route ran 1 h 56 min with steady I/O). On a breach the job's own gate_slot.py reports it on stderr and in the receipt, sends SIGTERM to its child and the descendants it started (each re-identified by start time through a pidfd), SIGKILL after 60 s, and exits 124 with `child_exit`; unreadable I/O counts as progress, and nothing outside the job's tree is signalled. (2) A rust-suite drain waits at most `--drain-timeout` (2 h, QUIRIN_GATE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT), then names each blocking holder (slot, pid, argv, hold time, CPU and I/O over the wait, resident set against admission), reopens admission, releases every lock it took and backs off 5 min so queued audits start; `--drain-attempts N` turns the Nth give-up into exit 75 before the command ran; the wait record stays `waiting` through back-offs (R7). (3) `gate_slot.py status [--json]` lists live holders, draining suites with their blockers, slot waiters and kernel-queued waiters from /proc/locks matched to the gate files' inodes, with wait and hold times, CPU and I/O over an interval and resident set against admission. (4) An audit job's tree resident set above its admission budget is reported while it runs (first crossing, then each further GiB) and kept in the receipt; the holder note carries the last sample. Tests: scripts/tests/test_gate_slot_starvation.py (26, scratch gate directories, spinning, sleeping, writing and allocating children) beside the 30 existing; an incident replay in a scratch gate (docs/reports/gate-slot-admission-starvation/replay.json): the queued audit ran in the drain's back-off, the spinner was stopped for its stall, the suite drained on its second attempt. The rule is stated in docs/agents/validation.md (Gate slots). No analyzer, contract, Lean or measure-plugin change; no measurement.

ledger.why: DISCHARGED by GATE-SLOT-ADMISSION-STARVATION (docs/reports/gate-slot-admission-starvation/README.md): (1) every slot job states a stall and wall-clock deadline in its receipt (audit default 2 h without any I/O, output, process change or progress-file change by its process tree, no wall-clock default; overridable by flag or QUIRIN_GATE_STALL_TIMEOUT / QUIRIN_GATE_DEADLINE) and on a breach its own gate_slot.py reports it on stderr and in the receipt and stops its own tree (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after the grace, exit 124), never another process; (2) a rust-suite drain waits at most --drain-timeout (2 h), then reopens admission, releases every lock it took, names each blocking holder with pid, argv, hold time, CPU and I/O over the wait and resident set against admission, and backs off and retries (--drain-attempts N fails with exit 75 before the command ran); (3) gate_slot.py status lists live holders and waiters from /proc/locks matched to the gate files' inodes with wait time, CPU and I/O deltas and resident set against admission; (4) an audit job's resident set above its admission budget is reported while it runs and kept in the receipt; tests in scratch gate directories (scripts/tests/test_gate_slot_starvation.py) and the rule in docs/agents/validation.md.

ledger.title: Review the slot deadline and drain defaults against the receipts
ledger.text: Registered by GATE-SLOT-ADMISSION-STARVATION. The defaults (audit stall 2 h, rust-suite drain 2 h, back-off 5 min, stop grace 60 s) were chosen from one measured pinned-corpus route (1 h 56 min with steady I/O) and the 2026-11-06 incident (10 h 18 min with zero I/O), not from a census. Before the card a drain admitted nothing until it finished; now each back-off lets queued audits start, so behind back-to-back long audits a rust-suite job can wait longer than the longest single audit. The receipts now record `limits`, `monitor` (samples, last progress, peak tree RSS, breach) and `slot_record.drain.attempts`. DISCHARGE: a review of a period of receipts (stalls, drains given up, rust-suite waits) with the defaults kept or changed by a recorded decision.

ledger.title: A declared measurement cannot override its routes' slot deadlines
ledger.text: Registered by GATE-SLOT-ADMISSION-STARVATION. The measure plugin clears each route's environment and passes only QUIRIN_GATE_DIR, QUIRIN_GATE_LEGACY_LOCK and QUIRIN_GATE_MEMINFO (crates/quirin-audit-plugin-measure/src/sides.rs GATE_VARIABLES), and runs `gate_slot.py audit` with fixed flags, so every route runs under the audit defaults (2 h stall, no wall-clock deadline) and a measurement whose route legitimately goes quiet longer has no override. DISCHARGE: the plugin forwards QUIRIN_GATE_STALL_TIMEOUT and QUIRIN_GATE_DEADLINE (or takes a flag) to gate_slot.py, records them in the route's run record, with a test.

ledger.title: gate_slot.py status does not list waiters that hold no gate lock
ledger.text: Registered by GATE-SLOT-ADMISSION-STARVATION. `gate_slot.py status` lists processes with a /proc/locks entry on a gate file: audit waiters show because they hold the legacy lock shared while they poll, and untimed legacy waiters are queued in the kernel. A job in a timed wait for the legacy lock (--wait-timeout while a `flock` legacy job holds it exclusive) holds nothing, and a nested job runs inside its parent's slot without a lock, so neither is listed. DISCHARGE: each slot job holds a lock on a per-job file under the gate directory from its first wait to its exit (or an equivalent the status reads), listed by status, with a test.

ledger.title: Slot stall, resident-set and status readings need /proc
ledger.text: Registered by GATE-SLOT-ADMISSION-STARVATION. The stall timeout, the resident-set report, `gate_slot.py status` and the drain's blocker CPU/I/O read /proc (/proc/<pid>/stat, io, cmdline, /proc/locks). Without it (macOS) the script says so and only the wall-clock deadline applies; status exits 1. Separately, the receipt's existing `max_rss_kib` reads wait4's ru_maxrss as KiB, which macOS reports in bytes. DISCHARGE: macOS readings (process tree, I/O and resident set through the platform's APIs, ru_maxrss scaled) with tests on that platform, or a recorded decision that the gate slots are Linux-only.
